title: add-benchmark-lab-performance-suites-reporting-pipeline-v143
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds v143 of benchmark-lab performance suites + reporting pipeline: new representative workload runners, profiling baselines for kernel-selection, and telemetry hooks for perf dashboards. No customer-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: update the benchmark lab to include v143 performance test suites, new profiling baselines for kernel-selection analysis, and a reporting pipeline that aggregates run results into the perf data warehouse. This PR wires representative workload runners for mixed CPU/GPU traces, improves profiler sampling to capture kernel selection heatmaps, and publishes standardized reporting artifacts consumed by the dashboard.

What changed (high level): - Added a new set of workload runners under benchmark-lab/workloads/mixed-v143 to better represent production chat and reranking traffic patterns. - Extended profiling baseline collection to capture kernel selection, memory watermarks, and kv-cache hit distributions. - New reporting pipeline components (etl/job definitions and templates) that normalize results into the perf schema and push to telemetry/warehouse. - Small runtime compatibility adapter to ensure samples from dedicated vs hosted runners look consistent to the reporting consumer.

Checklist: - [x] Representative workload runners implemented and unit-tested (local runner smoke) - [x] Profiling baselines collected for three model families (gpt-*-small/medium/large) - [x] Reporting pipeline jobs added and e2e tested in staging - [x] Telemetry hooks added to redact customer IDs and preserve cost metrics - [x] Docs and runbook updated (benchmark-lab/README + ops/perf-runbook)

Testing and verification: Ran the end-to-end pipeline in staging with 10 historical runs and synthetic load. Verified schema compatibility with infra/telemetry and validated dashboards refresh. CI runs include lint, unit tests, integration runner smoke, and telemetry ingestion tests. See CI checks below.

Rollout plan: Merge to main, deploy reporting ETL in staging for 48h, run nightly sample ingestion, validate dashboards and regression alerts, then promote ETL to prod during next maintenance window.

Notes: This change is backwards-compatible for existing reports. The new kernel-selection fields are additive; consumers not yet migrated will ignore them. Related: Linear ENG-1423 (profiling baselines), ENG-1487 (reporting pipeline normalization).

review_comments: Miguel Rivera: Nice work, this looks coherent with the adaptive-batching changes. Two requests: 1) add a small histogram of kernel selection in the integration smoke report, and 2) document the new fields in telemetry/schema/perf_runs_v2.sql.
Aisha Patel: Thanks Miguel — added histogram export to the smoke script and updated perf_runs_v2.sql with column comments (see commit a7b2d9f).
Samir Gupta: Can we ensure the baseline collector has a configurable sampling rate? At scale the default 100Hz caused overhead in a long run. Suggest exposing SAMPLE_RATE env var with sane defaults.
Aisha Patel: Exposed SAMPLE_RATE and added e2e test coverage that asserts overhead stays <1% for 1h synthetic runs.
